subject: Sprintbook: multi-wave go-live + canary windows (Stepwise Go-Live Playbook)

Subject: Sprintbook: multi-wave go-live + canary windows (Stepwise Go-Live Playbook)

Elena, team —

Congrats again on getting the contract across the finish line. Attached is the draft Sprintbook (MAP_Sprintbook_v1.xlsx) we promised during the close call. High-level intent: map a safe, observable path to full production across three waves (pilot, regional roll, global roll), with explicit canary windows, migration cutover, and two training micro-sprints before Wave 2.

Highlights and asks: 
- Wave 0 (pilot): 2-week canary, limited to 10% traffic, acceptance criteria = 99th < 350ms and no regression on the 50 eval prompts.
- Wave 1 (regional): 4-week phased ramp inside us-west, split into A/B cohorts.
- Wave 2 (global): final cutover, fallback policy to smaller quantized variant for burst protection.
- Pre-cutover dry run: we need a dry run for the full migration path (routing, cache warm, DB failover test) — propose 10/20.

Operational items we cover in the Sprintbook: canary checklist (Canary_Checklist.pdf), rollback checkpoints, KV/prefix cache warm-up plan, per-route latency SLOs, and training outlines for SOC/ops and product teams.

Please confirm the proposed dates in the sheet and attach any procurement/ops contacts we should loop in. I recommend we lock the dry run and the customer acceptance test (CAT) windows this week.

Attachments: MAP_Sprintbook_v1.xlsx (worksheet: Master Plan), Canary_Checklist.pdf

Thanks,

- We need a short, recorded training for our platform ops (two 45-min sessions) the week before Wave 1.
- On rollback: please document the customer-visible rollback message and DNS/TLS rollback plan — our comms team will want to pre-approve.

I added the procurement contact in the thread (procurement@blueharbor.com) for billing alignment and will upload our internal readiness doc to the Drive link you shared.

Agree with the shift to 10/25 for the dry run. A few operational additions I added inline in the Sprintbook: 
- KV/prefix cache warm-up: schedule warm-up jobs 48 hours before the dry run to populate common prefixes and embeddings cache. This reduces burst cold-start TTFB for the canary cohort.
- Quantization profile: for Wave 1 we recommend int8-pp for the non-critical batch endpoints; for low-latency frontdoor routes keep float16.
- Rollback automation: include a one-click fallback route that pins traffic to the smaller variant and triggers a ticket to oncall.
- Acceptance tests: automated eval harness (10 representative prompts) must pass with no >2% BLEU-quality drift versus baseline.

I updated the Confluence page with runbooks and playbook links: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/OPS/BH+Go-Live+Sprintbook (see Runbooks > Warmup & Rollback).

Attachments referenced: Canary_Checklist.pdf
